name: Kodika
product: Kodika Studio development build by Kodika.io Software Limited

evidence.says: The scanned bundle identifies version 2.5.5, a Kodika Dev icon and URL scheme, and a Debug server configuration.
Apple’s live Mac App Store metadata identifies public Kodika 3.6.0 under the separate production bundle ID mac.io.kodika.kodika.

limitation: The finding applies to the development build; the public Kodika Studio executable architecture was not established.
notes: Use the production bundle ID if creating a public Kodika Studio listing.

name: Unifying Installer
product: Logitech Unifying Installer, the installer for Logitech Unifying Software for Mac

evidence.says: The uploaded bundle identifies itself as Unifying Installer, with the exact bundle ID and CFBundleShortVersionString 1.3.
Logitech identifies the separately installed receiver-pairing utility as Logitech Unifying Software and says it is no longer maintained.

limitation: An exact release date for the scanned installer was not verified.
notes: The scanner displays 1.30 for the installer; Logitech's separate 1.3.375 package version is for the installed software distribution.

name: Paragon VMDK Mounter
product: Paragon VMDK Mounter for Mac OS X by Paragon Software Group

evidence.says: The official product page marks VMDK Mounter for Mac OS X as a legacy product unavailable since June 6, 2018.
Paragon's legacy statement lists VMDK Mounter for Mac OS X among the products discontinued on June 6, 2018.
The historical uploaded bundle records version 2.1370 and reports a single x86 architecture.

limitation: Paragon does not identify the final build number or its architecture on the legacy page, and the historical x86 scan does not establish that it was the final build.
notes: The scanner rounds 2.1370 to 2.14 in the listing header.

name: Pac-Bar

evidence.says: The developer ended personal support after macOS 10.15.6 Catalina, while leaving the open-source repository available for contributions.
The developer’s final release v1.3 provides the Pac-Bar_v1.3.zip artifact.
Inspection of Pac-Bar.app/Contents/MacOS/Pac-Bar and the accompanying Info.plist identified the matching v1.3 bundle and an x86_64-only Mach-O executable.

limitation: Apple Silicon runtime behavior was not verified.
notes: The final official build was Intel-only and remains downloadable.

name: Camtasia 3
product: Camtasia 3 for Mac by TechSmith Corporation

evidence.says: TechSmith’s current maintenance schedule covers recent Camtasia releases and has no maintenance for the legacy Camtasia 3 line.
TechSmith lists Camtasia 3.x among historical macOS releases and states Camtasia 2019.0.10 and earlier are unsupported on Apple Silicon.
The historical scan identifies the exact Camtasia 3 bundle version 3.1.7 as Intel x86.

limitation: No release date or independent Rosetta runtime test was verified for 3.1.7.
notes: This is the retired Camtasia 3 major version; newer Camtasia Editor releases have separate Apple Silicon support, and TechSmith still documents account-based redownload for legacy versions.

name: Uni Detector
product: Uni Detector by Takaaki Naganoya (Piyomaru Software)

evidence.says: Piyomaru Software's Mac App Store listing gives 1.2.1, released November 26, 2020, as the newest version.
The historical scan identifies the exact bundle ID and records x86 as the single architecture for version 1.2.1.
The author's executable inventory on macOS Tahoe reports that Uni Detector has only an x86_64 slice.
A March 2021 user report shows Uni Detector running on an M1 Mac mini with macOS 11.2.2 after version 1.2.1 was released.
After version 1.2.1 shipped, the developer reported that Uni Detector ran on Monterey in a discussion of their M1 benchmarks.

limitation: The M1 runtime report does not state the installed app build or explicitly show the translation mode.
notes: The reported Intel-only executable and separate M1 runtime report support the Rosetta disposition.

name: Automator
product: Automator, the workflow editor bundled with Apple macOS

evidence.says: Apple's current Automator User Guide documents the workflow editor and identifies product version 2.10 for macOS 27 Golden Gate in the page metadata.
RibbonMac's first-hand inspection identifies build 540 of Automator 2.10 in macOS 27 and reports arm64e slices in the main executable.
A separate hands-on guide reports running Automator 2.10 workflows on macOS 27.2.

limitation: The architecture is documented from a third-party inspection, and Apple does not publish a standalone release date for this Automator build.
notes: Version 2.10 is reused across macOS releases; the architecture claim covers the macOS 27 build described in the evidence.

name: pdpop download client
product: PDPop Download Client for Mac by Gvix, distributed by PDPop (TBENM)

evidence.says: PDPop says PDPopDownClient cannot run independently and opens to handle downloads initiated on the PDPop website.
PDPop provides the Mac client package and documents how the helper opens site downloads from supported browsers.
Inspection of PDPopDownClient.app/Contents/MacOS/PDPopDownClient and its Info.plist inside the official package identified v2.0.9 with both x86_64 and arm64 Mach-O slices.

limitation: The release date and runtime behavior of v2.0.9 were not verified.
notes: The current download helper has a universal executable.

name: iBeesoft Data Recovery
product: iBeesoft Data Recovery for Mac by iBeesoft

evidence.says: iBeesoft advertises Mac version 6.6 and links to its official disk image.
The linked disk image contains the matching v6.5 com.ibeesoft.datarecovery bundle, whose main executable has x86_64 and arm64 Mach-O slices.

limitation: Architecture of the separately advertised v6.6 and the release date of the downloaded v6.5 were not verified.
notes: The DMG served by the vendor contained v6.5 build 6500 in the nested iBeesoft Data Recovery.app/Contents/MacOS/iBeesoft Data Recovery executable, and the enclosing v6.5 iBeesoftLoader is universal as well.

name: SWClient
product: 顺网云电脑 (Shunwang Cloud PC) macOS desktop client by Shunwang Technology

evidence.says: Shunwang offers a distinct desktop macOS client alongside its iOS app and web service.
The official download page’s public package lookup returns the Mac ZIP as its current Mac package and dates that package July 28, 2026.
Inside the official ZIP’s DMG, inspection identified 顺网云电脑.app/Contents/MacOS/SWClient as universal x86_64 and arm64, with bundle version 2026-07-23,11:26:30 and ID com.shunwang.swClient.
The original scan names the main executable SWClient and contains the same Chinese product name and microphone permission text as the current vendor bundle.

limitation: Static inspection established the main executable architecture; runtime and auxiliary executables were not tested.
notes: The old bundle ID was an unresolved build placeholder; use com.shunwang.swClient as its current identifier. The vendor download API labels the package v4.1.2, its ZIP filename says v4.0.0, and the app’s own version is a timestamp. To reproduce the package lookup, POST {"agencyAlias":"guanwang"} as application/json with the Shunwang download page as the referer.

name: touchbar_nyancat

evidence.says: The maintainer’s latest release 0.3.0 announces M1 compatibility.
Inspection of touchbar_nyancat.app/Contents/MacOS/touchbar_nyancat and its Info.plist in the 0.3.0 release ZIP identified the matching bundle with an x86_64-only Mach-O executable.
The proposed native ARM changes remain open and unmerged.

limitation: Rosetta compatibility follows from the maintainer’s M1 claim and the Intel-only build, without a local runtime test.
notes: The public tag is 0.3.0 while the app’s CFBundleShortVersionString is 1.0. The advertised animation displays on the MacBook Pro Touch Bar.

name: TouchBrickout

evidence.says: The developer identifies TouchBrickout as the release name of TouchBreakout and links to the package.
The project’s latest packaged release is v1.1, published November 21, 2017.
Inspection of TouchBrickout.app/Contents/MacOS/TouchBrickout and its Info.plist from the official package identified the matching v1.1 bundle and an x86_64-only Mach-O executable.

limitation: No product-specific evidence established whether the v1.1 package runs under Rosetta.
notes: The game supports keyboard controls and Touch Bar input.

name: Unplug Alarm
product: Unplug Alarm: Anti-theft App for macOS by Apprime Studio sarl

evidence.says: Apple’s live storefront metadata identifies Apprime Studio’s current Mac release as bundle app.unplugalarm.mac version 1.8.1, released September 28, 2026.
Softpedia’s Mac software catalog explicitly classifies the same 1.8.1 release as a Universal Binary.

limitation: The architecture statement comes from an independent Mac software catalog, and the current App Store binary was not inspected.
notes: This is the Apprime Studio Mac anti-theft app with App Store ID 1489026302, distinct from the same-named open-source app and from Apprime’s mobile companion.

name: MDB Explorer
product: MDB Explorer for Mac by GrandSoft Ltd.

evidence.says: The historical launch article identifies GrandSoft’s Mac app and links the original App Store ID 506622388 and vendor disk-image address.
Apple’s live US storefront lookup returns zero results for the historical App Store ID.
The original vendor download endpoint serves an HTML redirect to a domain-parking landing page instead of a disk image.
The historical catalog for the exact bundle ID records version 2.4.7 with a June 24, 2016 update date.
The archived scan of GrandSoft’s Mac bundle version 2.4.7 reports Intel slices and no arm64 slice.

limitation: The end of distribution is inferred from the former store and vendor channels; no vendor retirement announcement or Rosetta runtime test was found.
notes: Apple also returned zero results for the exact app ID in France, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong. GrandSoft’s similarly named ACCDB MDB Explorer had a different App Store ID.
